newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on soybean losses, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on soybean losses, weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended lower on Wednesday after soybeans posted limit losses with forecasts for warmer weather adding to the bearish mood, traders said.
Soybeans collapsed after Cargill Inc confirmed it was importing Brazilian soybeans for use at southeastern U.S. processing plants.

The move was also termed bearish for corn, which competes with soymeal as a feed ingredient. Trade sources noted the imports would likely erode soymeal basis levels in the southeast, reducing the likelihood that poultry and pork producers would feed corn instead.
Reports that Brazilian crusher Ceval Alimentos was negotiating to sell 40,000 tonnes of soymeal to the U.S. added to ideas corn demand in the Southeast would fade.
Weather forecasts further weakened new crop.
Forecasters predicted a brief warm up early next week for the eastern U.S. Midwest. Corn had rallied on Tuesday on concerns persistent cool, wet weather would hamper early crop development.
Corn ended 6-1/4 to three cents per bushel lower with July off 6-1/4 at $2.71-1/4 and new crop December down five cents at $2.54-3/4.
Funds were aggressive sellers of at least 20 million bushels on the day. Several trade sources said the sales were likely new positions rather than long liquidation.
FIMAT Futures sold 5.5 million bushels December, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer sold four million December and Tenco Inc sold two million each July and December, traders said.
Cargill Investor Services and Dean Witter bearh spread one million bushels December/July at 18 cents, premium July.

Options trade was again active with CIS a seller of 1,100 December $2.30 puts at four cents, floor sources said. Tenco Inc bought 500 December $2.70 calls at 12 to 11-3/4 cents and sold 500 December $2.40 puts at seven cents.
Farmers Commodities Corp and Refco Inc each bought 500 July $3.10 calls at 1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 85,000 contracts, above Tuesday's actual volume of 52,931.
